## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double anonymized: reviewer and author identities concealed from each other. After an initial evaluation (out-of-scope or unsuitable manuscripts may be desk rejected without review), two independent reviews are required for a revise or accept decision, except that Agora pieces and media reviews may not need two. Reviewers interact with the editor; no review information is published. Source: submission guidelines, Wayback copy 2025-07-06, https://web.archive.org/web/20250706132609/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/oss; retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No transfer scheme found on the pages read. The aims page copy of 2024-04-07 says that in the medium term the journal will advise authors of manuscripts that draw on no empirical data in any form to submit to its sibling journal Organization Theory instead (see Format) |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | No. The guidelines copy states "Review information published: None" (same URL as above) |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Blank. SciRev's single full-review report lists 1.0 round (n=1, a rejection), which says nothing about revise-and-resubmit practice (https://scirev.org/journal/organization-studies/) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Not accepted: the guidelines say the journal assigns reviewers and cannot accept author recommendations. Editors and senior editors make the final decision. The journal uses editorial-board and editorial-review-board members as reviewers, at most one per manuscript from that pool, then reaches beyond it (same guidelines copy) |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | No journal-specific text found. The journal's guidelines (copy 2025-07-06) only say AI chatbots such as ChatGPT must not be listed as authors and refer to the publisher's policy on generative AI tools. The publisher-wide Sage policy applies |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate found. Use is allowed with disclosure |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed with mandatory disclosure; this pass's own rubric, same as the other AI-researched entries) |
| **Summary** | Sage policy as archived 2024-05-30: authors must state in the methods or acknowledgements which model was used and for what, verify the accuracy of generated content and citations, and watch for reproduced text; AI bots cannot be authors; the publisher says it will take corrective action on published articles with undisclosed use. Editors must not share manuscripts or review reports with generative AI, and reviewers must not use AI tools to write review reports. The policy page itself notes it may evolve, so the live wording may differ. Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Source URL** | https://web.archive.org/web/20240530222352/https://www.sagepub.com/en-us/nam/chatgpt-and-generative-ai (live page 403) and the journal guidelines copy https://web.archive.org/web/20250706132609/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/oss |

| Stage | Allowed? | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|

| Post-acceptance (AAM) | Yes | The archiving page says the original submission or accepted manuscript may be shared at any time after acceptance, on any website, repository or social channel; no embargo period appears in the text read. | Version of Record | Limited | The archiving page (Wayback copy 2024-07-22) itemises four permitted uses of the final published PDF: in relation to the author's own teaching (with restricted electronic access), sharing on an individual basis with research colleagues for non-commercial purposes, in the author's dissertation or thesis (including posting in an institutional repository), and in a book authored or edited by the author, at any time after publication in the journal; it may not be posted on an unrestricted website or repository without Sage's permission. Open access articles are covered by their licence |

## Format

> Source for every row: the journal's aims page (Wayback copy 2024-04-07) and submission guidelines (Wayback copy 2025-07-06), both listed under Identity; live pages return 403, so current wording may differ. The word limits below appear identically in both copies. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Six types listed: empirical or conceptual research articles; shorter essay-style "X and Organization Studies"; Perspectives articles (introductions to virtual special issues); Method/ology articles; Agora opinion pieces; media reviews. Research articles, X and OS essays, Perspectives and Method/ology articles are peer reviewed. Both archived pages accept conceptual work: the aims copy of 2024-04-07 says "we accept conceptual articles that develop theory without reliance on empirical data", and the visible text of the guidelines copy of 2025-07-06 says "We welcome empirical and conceptual research articles". The same aims paragraph adds that "in the medium term" the journal will focus on empirical manuscripts and advise authors of manuscripts that draw on no empirical data in any form to submit to Organization Theory; this is a stated direction, not a rule that conceptual articles are refused. A search-engine summary of the live guidelines (secondary, unverified; the live page returns 403 and the archived 2025-07-06 copy, which is later than June 2025, does not contain the wording) says that from June 2025 only empirical research articles are welcomed; that summary is contradicted by the 2025-07-06 visible text and is not used |
| **Word limit** | Research articles: 13,000 words including references and appendices. X and Organization Studies essays: 7,500 words including references. Perspectives: 13,000 including references. Method/ology articles: 13,000 including references. Agora: 2,000 words in total including references, single-authored |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. The pages state maxima without exceptions. X and OS, Perspectives and Agora pieces require discussing the idea with the editors-in-chief first |
| **Abstract limit** | Unstructured abstract, 300 words maximum; keywords: a minimum of 5-7, of which four must come from the journal's submission-system keyword list; an author biography of at most 100 words per author is entered at submission |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap; references count inside the word limits above. Style: the visible guidelines text (copy 2025-07-06) says only to follow the OS Style and Reference Guide; a sentence naming the "Sage Harvard" style exists in the archived HTML only inside an HTML comment (template text, not policy), so Sage Harvard is not recorded as a requirement |
| **Supplementary material** | Allowed: the journal can host supplemental files (datasets, video, images) alongside the article |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Figures at 300 dpi; colour is free online and charged only if print colour is requested (guidelines copy) |
| **Anonymisation and other submission rules** | Manuscript must be fully anonymised with identifying information moved to a separate title page; the title page also carries ethics, funding, conflict and data statements. A rejected manuscript may not be resubmitted unless an editor invites it; the editors consider at most three submissions at a time from one author; Agora authors cannot resubmit an Agora for three years after acceptance of a published one (guidelines and aims copies) |

### Orientation

> Counts come from Crossref records of this journal published 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23: 583 journal-article records (book and media reviews included), of which 398 (68.3%) carry an abstract. A hit is a record with an abstract whose title or abstract matches the regular expression (case-insensitive, word boundaries; every expression is in the keyword register in the AI-Research Notes); shares use 398 as the denominator. Counts are lower bounds because 185 records have no abstract. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Empirical designs dominate by keyword: "qualitative-any" (qualitative, case study, ethnograph*, interview) 170 of 398 abstract records (42.7%) against "theory-building-any" (conceptual, theorizing, essay, theory building) 70 (17.6%); the two can overlap in one record. The aims copy of 2024-04-07 says the journal encourages the interplay of theorizing and empirical research and states a medium-term focus on empirical manuscripts |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Qualitative leads: "qualitative" 60 (15.1%), "case study" 48 (12.1%), "ethnograph*" 47 (11.8%), "interview" 39 (9.8%) against "quantitative-survey-any" 10 (2.5%) and "experimental" 16 (4.0%) |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | The journal describes itself as multidisciplinary, rooted in the social sciences, open to a wide range of philosophical traditions, disciplines and methodological approaches (aims copy 2024-04-07). Sage files it under "Management and Organization Studies" on its discipline list (journal home copy 2025-08-05) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes, a theory-contribution framing is stated by the journal: every article must engage seriously with the existing literature, clearly say which conversations it joins or challenges and what novel theoretical insight it adds in relation to organizational literatures; each article needs "solid theoretical grounding". Source: aims page, Wayback copy 2024-04-07, https://web.archive.org/web/20240407171513/https://journals.sagepub.com/aims-scope/oss. Retrieved 2026-11-23.
- **What kind of engagement?** Empirical submissions must account for and motivate the approach chosen and show rigour in data collection and analysis appropriate to it (same aims page). The journal states it is open to paradigmatic plurality but not to novelty as an end in itself.
- **Article types and lengths:** see Format (research articles 13,000 words incl. references; X and OS 7,500; Method/ology 13,000; Perspectives 13,000; Agora 2,000). The cover letter is asked to say why the manuscript suits the journal and should not summarise the paper (guidelines copy 2025-07-06, https://web.archive.org/web/20250706132609/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/oss).
- **Current scope signal:** the aims copy (2024-04-07) accepts conceptual articles and the guidelines copy (2025-07-06) welcomes empirical and conceptual research articles, while the aims page also says the journal will in the medium term focus on empirical manuscripts and advise manuscripts that draw on no empirical data in any form to submit to Organization Theory; a search summary says this became a strict rule from June 2025 (unverified and contradicted by the 2025-07-06 visible text; see Format). Special issues and virtual special issues are listed on the journal home copy of 2025-08-05 (https://web.archive.org/web/20250805123023/https://journals.sagepub.com/home/oss); no current call text was read.
- **Consequences of ignoring it:** the guidelines say manuscripts outside scope or of insufficient quality are not reviewed and may be desk rejected (guidelines copy). No data on what share is desk rejected exists beyond 5 of 6 SciRev reports (https://scirev.org/reviews/organization-studies/).

### Methodological Preferences

> Scores follow this pass's own convention, not an external standard: share of the 398 abstract records (2021-2026, Crossref) whose title or abstract matches the expression; 0 hits = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement. None was found: the aims text says the journal accepts qualitative, quantitative or mixed methods and conceptual articles, and states no ranking of methods, so no row exceeds 3. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how reviewers judge it. The schema's rows were kept where they fit; rows that do not fit a management venue are said so below. Expressions are in the register in the AI-Research Notes.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Qualitative case study | 3 | "case study" 48 of 398 (12.1%); "qualitative" 60 (15.1%); "qualitative-any" 170 (42.7%). Aims copy 2024-04-07: open to qualitative, quantitative or mixed methods |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored. Observation from the 398 abstracts (Crossref, 2021-2026): 367 (92.2%) contain a first-person word (I, my, we, our), nearly all plural; 21 (5.3%) contain singular I or my. Among 45 single-author records with an abstract, 20 use singular I or my and 28 use any first-person form. Newest examples with first person: https://doi.org/10.1177/01708406261511702 and https://doi.org/10.1177/01708406261511695. The guidelines read give no rule on first person (guidelines copy 2025-07-06). Plural "we" may be a convention of collective authorship rather than a stance |
| **Expected density** | Length ceiling 13,000 words including references (guidelines copy). No article-length statistics were gathered |
| **Abstract and keywords** | Unstructured abstract up to 300 words; 5-7 keywords at minimum, four of them from the journal's list (guidelines copy) |
| **Writing style notes** | References follow the journal's own OS Style and Reference Guide (the visible text names no other style; a "Sage Harvard" sentence appears only inside an HTML comment in the archived page, so it is not recorded); Word is the preferred format and no template is required (a sentence saying LaTeX files are also accepted appears only inside an HTML comment, template text, not recorded as policy); every citation must match the reference list; citations to preprints are discouraged once a peer-reviewed version exists (guidelines copy 2025-07-06). The aims page asks authors to say which conversations they join and what the novel theoretical contribution is (aims copy 2024-04-07). Article section order was not sampled |
| **Authorship pattern** | Crossref author counts over 583 records (book and media reviews included): 1 author 191, 2 authors 166, 3 authors 143, 4 or more 83 (retrieved 2026-11-23). Singly authored records are therefore 32.8% of the records |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewer behaviour itself is not observable from public pages; what follows is what public pages do show.

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Dominant tradition** | The board page lists 2 editors-in-chief, 33 senior editors, 4 media review editors, 1 managing editor, 12 former editors-in-chief and 220 editorial-board entries (272 entries). The guidelines say the journal has an Editorial Board and an Editorial Review Board serving as external reviewers; only the Editorial Board list was on the page copy read | Board copy 2025-05-27: https://web.archive.org/web/20250527060146/https://journals.sagepub.com/editorial-board/oss ; guidelines copy 2025-07-06; retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Reviewer list size** | 220 editorial-board entries on the page; countries by entry sum to 220 (UK 64, France 19, USA 18, Canada 18, Australia 17, Netherlands 14, Denmark 12, Germany 11, Switzerland 7, Sweden 5, Finland 5, Italy 4, Austria 4, Israel 4, Spain 4, New Zealand 2, Norway 2, China 2, Ireland 2, Brazil, Mexico, Portugal, Luxembourg and Japan 1 each, 1 with no country printed). The Editorial Review Board is not listed on the copy read | Same board copy |
| **Review model** | Double anonymized; two independent reviews required for revise or accept; reviewers interact with the editor; reports not published | Guidelines copy 2025-07-06 |
| **Reviewer competence variance** | Blank. No first-hand report beyond SciRev's n=6: one full-review report rates report quality 2.0 of 5 (n=1), one immediate-rejection report says the editor may have skimmed the paper's introduction, one praises extensive editorial comments (paraphrased) | https://scirev.org/reviews/organization-studies/ |
| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Blank. No source. Qualitative designs are the most frequent in the journal's abstracts (170 of 398, 42.7%), which does not show how reviewers treat any design | Crossref counts, see Methodological Preferences |

Of the 33 senior editors, 9 print UK, 5 Canada, 4 USA; six exact names (Alaimo, Bapuji, Roulet, Wenzel, Foroughi, Hwang) appear in both a senior or media list and the board list. Author side: UK 221, France 98, US 80 of 582 works (OpenAlex) | Board copy 2025-05-27; OpenAlex group_by authorships.countries, retrieved 2026-11-23 |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | Stated by the journal: all papers reporting studies with human participants, human data or human tissue must state that the relevant ethics committee approved the study or waived approval, with the committee's full name, institution and approval number; an ethics section sits on the title page under "Statements and Declarations", and "not applicable" must be stated explicitly where relevant (guidelines copy 2025-07-06, https://web.archive.org/web/20250706132609/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/oss). Consent to participate and consent for publication statements are also required there |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author records are common: 191 of 583 Crossref records (32.8%), and 45 of the 398 records with abstracts (Crossref, 2021-2026). Agora pieces must be single-authored (guidelines copy) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Blank for any rule or count. The guidelines ask for the affiliation where the research was conducted and say nothing on unaffiliated authors (guidelines copy 2025-07-06); the board page does not label anyone independent |
| **Data transparency requirement** | Encouraged, not mandated in the text read: authors are encouraged to share data in a public repository and include a data availability statement linking to it or explaining why sharing is impossible; the title page template lists a data availability statement (guidelines copy 2025-07-06) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double anonymized, with the manuscript fully anonymised and identifying information on a separate title page not sent to reviewers; the cover letter should name people who have seen the paper and colleagues with conflicts. A preprint is allowed before submission but must not be updated during review (guidelines copy 2025-07-06) |
| **AI use** | AI cannot be an author; disclosure of model and purpose required under the publisher policy (archived 2024-05-30, https://web.archive.org/web/20240530222352/https://www.sagepub.com/en-us/nam/chatgpt-and-generative-ai) |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid, no submission or page fee; optional open access fee via Sage Choice, amount not read (OpenAlex lists USD 3900 / GBP 2859, unverified). 285 of 582 works from 2021-2026 are hybrid open access in OpenAlex |
| **Other submission rules** | Maximum three submissions at a time from one author; no resubmission of a rejected paper unless an editor invites it (guidelines copy 2025-07-06) |

### AI-Research Notes (sources, blanks, and cross-language checks)

**signal_quality (0-5)**: overall 3. Per layer: Crossref keyword counts (methods, topics, voice) 3 (583 records, 68.3% with abstracts, counts are lower bounds); OpenAlex metrics and country counts 4; publisher-wide policies 3 (Wayback copies dated 2024); journal-specific policies and guidelines 3 (Wayback copies of the aims page 2024-04-07, board 2025-05-27, home 2025-08-05 and guidelines 2025-07-06 are the journal's own text but one to two years old; live pages unreadable); experiential layer 1 (SciRev n=6, self-selected, no calendar dates).

**Per-subsection state (for the promotion gate)**: Epistemological, Methodological Preferences, Sensitive Topics, Reviewer Pool and Practical Concerns rest on counts or archived journal pages; Framing Requirements rests on the aims page copy; Voice & Style rests on abstract counts and archived guidelines but has no sample of article openings beyond abstracts. Reviewer behaviour, review time beyond n=6 and acceptance rate stay blank.

**Method.** Crossref records: `https://api.crossref.org/journals/0170-8406/works` (also via `works?filter=issn:0170-8406,from-pub-date:2021-01-01,until-pub-date:2026-11-23`, cursor paging, fields DOI, title, abstract, type, published, subject, author). 583 records, all of type journal-article, 398 with abstracts. Abstract HTML tags were stripped. Each keyword was matched with a Python regular expression, case-insensitive, over title plus abstract, counting a record once; shares divide by 398. Title-only counts run over all 583 titles. OpenAlex counts use group_by queries on `primary_location.source.issn:0170-8406,publication_year:2021-2026` (582 works), no key or email, single requests. The first-person expressions are case-sensitive: any first person `\b(?:I|[Mm]y|[Ww]e|[Oo]ur)\b`, singular `\b(?:I|[Mm]y)\b`.

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Scope and theory contribution**: the aims copy states every article must engage seriously with the literature and state its novel theoretical contribution, and the guidelines say out-of-scope or insufficient-quality manuscripts are not reviewed (Framing Requirements; guidelines copy 2025-07-06).
- **Empirical-focus signal (not a stated block)**: the aims copy of 2024-04-07 accepts conceptual articles and the guidelines copy of 2025-07-06 welcomes empirical and conceptual research articles, but the aims page says that in the medium term the journal will focus on empirical manuscripts and advise those drawing on no empirical data in any form to submit to Organization Theory; a search summary of a stricter June 2025 rule is unverified and contradicted by the 2025-07-06 text (Format). A paper with no empirical data therefore carries a stated redirect risk, not a stated prohibition.
- **Length**: 13,000 words including references and appendices for research articles (Format); no exception stated.
- **Anonymisation**: the manuscript must be fully anonymised with a separate title page (Format, Practical Concerns).
- **Process rules**: no resubmission after rejection without an editor's invitation, and at most three concurrent submissions per author (Format).
- **AI use**: undisclosed generative AI use breaches the publisher policy; AI cannot be an author (AI Policy).

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: the only turnaround data are SciRev's n=6 (immediate rejections after 7 to 52 days; one full-review rejection after 18.0 weeks); no time-to-acceptance exists (Review Cycle Time).
- **Preprint constraint**: a preprint may not be updated while the manuscript is under review (Preprint Policy).
- **Open access cost**: gold open access costs an APC whose amount was not read (OpenAlex lists USD 3900 / GBP 2859, unverified; Open Access).
- **Length of theory framing**: because the journal demands an explicit theoretical contribution and positioning in conversations (Framing Requirements), a data-first paper carries the cost of writing that positioning even within the 13,000-word ceiling.

### Best Suited For

- Qualitative, field-based organization research that builds theory from data: case study 12.1%, ethnography 11.8% and interviews 9.8% of abstract records (Methodological Preferences).
- Work on institutions, power, paradox, identity or sustainability, which appear in 14.1%, 18.3%, 7.0%, 6.5% and 10.6% of abstract records (Epistemological, Sensitive Topics).
- Archival or historical empirical studies (6.3%) and longitudinal designs (7.5%) (Methodological Preferences).
- Essay-style provocations through the "X and Organization Studies" and Agora sections, after discussion with the editors (Format: 7,500 and 2,000 words).
- Authors who want a double-anonymised process (Peer Review).

### Not Recommended For

- Papers that draw on no empirical data in any form: conceptual articles are accepted on the pages read, but the aims page states a medium-term redirect of such manuscripts to Organization Theory, so they carry a stated risk rather than a bar (Format; Hard Blockers). Conceptual vocabulary appears in 23 of 398 abstract records (5.8%) (Methodological Preferences).
- Primarily quantitative, survey-based or experimental work: 2.5% and 4.0% of abstract records (Methodological Preferences); the counts show these are uncommon here, not that they are rejected, and the aims copy accepts quantitative methods.
- Literature reviews and meta-analyses: 0 of 398 abstract records (Methodological Preferences).
- Anyone needing a verified turnaround or acceptance rate before choosing: none exists in the sources read (Metrics, Review Cycle Time).

### Rejection Fallback Chain

> No source states where rejected authors usually go. The rows below are topical neighbours, chosen because they share the subject area (management and organization studies) and, for rank 3, because the journal's own aims page names it; they are not a claim about acceptance odds.

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Human Relations](human-relations.md) | Same subject area; an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
| 2 | [Journal of Management Studies](journal-of-management-studies.md) | Same subject area; an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
| 3 | Organization Theory (Sage) | Named on this journal's own aims page (copy 2024-04-07) as the destination the journal will in the medium term advise for manuscripts that draw on no empirical data in any form; not in this corpus |
